description:
=== DONE (s473t5d) ===
FOUND + FIXED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5.

`use bytes` is a no-op in PCL by design (docs/not-supported.md
"### `use bytes` -- byte view of upgraded strings"), but bytes.pm also exports
CALLABLE names, and `bytes::length($s)` is one real code writes:

  t/io/utf8.t:201  tell(F) == ($a += bytes::length($b))
  Text::CSV_PP.pm:1878/1884  $cache->{sep_len} / {quo_len}

With the sub missing the call was `Undefined subroutine &BYTES::length` --
an abort that killed the rest of the form and stopped t/io/utf8.t at 27 of 62.

WHERE IT LIVES, and why: a `:bytes` package in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, beside the
`:utf8` one.  Rule 9a's question ("could a user write this in plain Perl?")
answers NO here: the value is a statement about the SV's INTERNAL form, and a
plain-Perl shim would have to ask `utf8::is_utf8`, which PCL hardcodes to 1
(see that function's own comment) -- every string would take the octet branch.
`bytes` is a CORE pragma, not a module, so the smell test passes exactly as
`utf8::encode` does.

PERL'S RULE, probed 5.40.3 over fourteen shapes, is
`utf8::is_utf8($s) ? <utf8 octet count> : length($s)`.  PCL has no UTF8 flag;
the stand-in is "a character above 255 has no octet form, so measure as UTF-8;
otherwise the string IS its octets".  That agrees with perl on
ascii(3) latin-1(1) chr(130)=1 chr(255)=1 chr(256)=2 chr(300)=2 mixed(5)
empty(0) NUL(2) U+2019(3) U+10000(4) a number(5) and undef(0).

THE ONE DIVERGENCE: an ARTIFICIALLY upgraded latin-1 string
(`$s="\xa3\xff"; utf8::upgrade($s)`) is 4 in perl and 2 here -- the upgrade PCL
cannot represent is exactly the fact the answer would need.  It is the same
no-UTF8-flag gap the `use bytes` section already records, and the guard row
asserts PCL's 2 with that note so the row says where the model stops.

RESULT: t/io/utf8.t 23/4 -> 53/9 (30 blessed fail rows + 35 shortfall rows left
the baselines by EDIT).  Guard Pl/t/io-layers-01.t row 39.  No emission change.

NOT DONE: the other bytes.pm functions (`bytes::substr`, `chr`, `ord`, `index`,
`rindex`).  Measured: `bytes::length` is the ONLY one used anywhere in perl's
t/, PCL's perl-tests/, lib/ or cpan-tests/ (grep -a over all four), so they are
added when something asks for them.
subject: `bytes::length` -- the callable half of the `bytes` pragma -- was undefined, so an undef-fn abort took the whole top-level form (t/io/utf8.t and Text::CSV_PP)
